what_it_is.prose: GA-ASI is the manufacturer of the Predator/MQ-9 family of HALE UAVs and is now a top-tier India defence partner following the October 2024 signing of a $3.9 billion (≈₹32,000 crore) contract for 31 MQ-9B SkyGuardian/SeaGuardian HALE RPAS for the Indian tri-services (16 Army, 8 Navy, 7 Air Force). Deliveries are expected between 2027 and 2030. India had previously leased two MQ-9B SeaGuardians for the Indian Navy in 2020, and signed a follow-on ₹1,943 crore lease for two additional SeaGuardians in August 2026 (delivered soon after). GA-ASI opened its India office in New Delhi in November 2018, has a strategic partnership with Bharat Forge (Jan 2023) for aerostructures, an MOU with HAL (Feb 2023) for MQ-9B engine MRO support, and an MOU with Huneed Technologies for flat panel array supply.

faq.question: What is the size of India's MQ-9B Predator deal with General Atomics?
faq.answer: India signed a $3.9 billion (≈₹32,000 crore) contract in October 2024 for 31 MQ-9B SkyGuardian/SeaGuardian HALE RPAS — 16 for the Indian Army, 8 for the Indian Navy and 7 for the Indian Air Force. The US State Department approved the FMS sale on 1 February 2024 and deliveries are expected between 2027 and 2030.

faq.question: When did General Atomics open its India office?
faq.answer: General Atomics Global opened its India office in New Delhi on 27 November 2018, simultaneously announcing the appointment of an Indian executive (Dr. Vivek Lall) to lead India strategic affairs.

faq.question: Which Indian companies have partnerships with GA-ASI for MQ-9B?
faq.answer: GA-ASI has a strategic partnership with Bharat Forge (Kalyani Group), announced 3 January 2023, to manufacture aerostructures in India; an MOU with HAL (Feb 2023) for MQ-9B engine MRO support; and an MOU with Huneed Technologies for flat-panel array supply.
